## Why This Is Asked

Static-site serving in a per-namespace context tests PVC/ConfigMap/Secret integration, nginx config via ConfigMap, and safe multi-tenant limits with quotas and limits.

## Key Concepts

- Deployments, replicas, and rolling updates
- PVCs for shared data, ConfigMaps for content and nginx.conf, Secrets for credentials
- nginx basic auth integration via config map
- ClusterIP Service exposure and Readiness/Liveness probes
- Namespace ResourceQuota and LimitRange for multi-tenant safety

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal skeleton showing core resources
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: site-content
data:
  index.html: |-
    <html>...</html>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: nginx-config
data:
  nginx.conf: |
    server { listen 80; location / { auth_basic "Restricted"; auth_basic_user_file /etc/nginx/.htpasswd; root /usr/share/nginx/html; } }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: basic-auth
type: Opaque
data:
  # base64(encoded username:password)
  htpasswd: <base64>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: static-site
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:stable
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        volumeMounts:
        - name: site
          mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
        - name: config
          mountPath: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
          subPath: nginx.conf
        - name: auth
          mountPath: /etc/nginx/.htpasswd
          subPath: htpasswd
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: site
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: static-site-pvc
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: nginx-config
      - name: auth
        secret:
          secretName: basic-auth
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: static-site-svc
spec:
  selector:
    app: static-site
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 80
    protocol: TCP
  type: ClusterIP
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: static-site-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to safely patch CronJobs, leverage InitContainers for bootstrapping from ConfigMaps, enforce security context non-root, and apply sensible history limits. It also probes operational testing and rollback strategy for scheduled jobs.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob controls: concurrencyPolicy, history limits, startingDeadlineSeconds
- InitContainers and ConfigMaps for bootstrapping
- PodSecurityContext: runAsNonRoot
- Probes on Jobs' pods and resource requests/limits
- Testing and rollback of scheduled jobs

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal CronJob patch outline (conceptual)
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: db-backup
  namespace: nightly
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 3600
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: backup-sa
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
          initContainers:
            - name: init-backup
              image: busybox
              command: ["sh", "-c", "cp /config/backup.sh /backup/backup.sh"]
              volumeMounts:
                - name: backup-config
                  mountPath: /config
                - name: backups
                  mountPath: /backup
          containers:
            - name: backup
              image: backup-tool:latest
              resources:
                requests:
                  memory: "128Mi"
                  cpu: "100m"
                limits:
                  memory: "256Mi"
                  cpu: "500m"
              readinessProbe:
                httpGet:
                  path: /livez
                  port: 8080
              livenessProbe:
                httpGet:
                  path: /readyz
                  port: 8080
              volumeMounts:
                - name: backups
                  mountPath: /backups
          volumes:
            - name: backups
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: backups-pvc
            - name: backup-config
              configMap:
                name: backup-config
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests CKAD fundamentals in a realistic nightly QA workflow: CronJobs, per-namespace isolation, PVC usage, ConfigMap/Secret mounts, InitContainer dependency management, TLS rotation sidecar, health probes, and restrictive NetworkPolicy. Also evaluates data validation patterns and architectural trade-offs.

## Key Concepts

- CronJob scheduling and namespace isolation
- PVC data persistence and volume mounting
- ConfigMap/Secret mounting and environment injection
- InitContainer for runtime dependency installation
- Sidecar pattern for TLS certificate rotation
- Readiness/Liveness probe implementation
- NetworkPolicy egress restrictions
- Python data validation with pandas/jsonschema

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: data-qa-cronjob
  namespace: example
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: install-deps
            image: python:3.9-alpine
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              pip install pandas==1.3.3 jsonschema==3.2.0 --target /app/deps
            volumeMounts:
            - name: deps-volume
              mountPath: /app/deps
          containers:
          - name: validator
            image: python:3.9-alpine
            command:
            - python
            - -c
            - |
              import sys
              sys.path.append('/app/deps')
              import os
              import pandas as pd
              import jsonschema
              import requests
              from datetime import datetime
              
              schema_path = os.getenv('SCHEMA_PATH', '/data/schema.json')
              date_range = os.getenv('DATE_RANGE', '7')
              
              # Load schema
              with open(schema_path) as f:
                  schema = json.load(f)
              
              # Validate CSVs
              for csv_file in os.listdir('/data'):
                  if csv_file.endswith('.csv'):
                      df = pd.read_csv(f'/data/{csv_file}')
                      try:
                          jsonschema.validate(df.to_dict('records'), schema)
                          result = {'file': csv_file, 'status': 'pass', 'timestamp': datetime.utcnow().isoformat()}
                      except Exception as e:
                          result = {'file': csv_file, 'status': 'fail', 'error': str(e), 'timestamp': datetime.utcnow().isoformat()}
                      
                      # Send to QA portal
                      requests.post('http://qa-portal:8090/api/v1/qa', 
                                   json=result,
                                   headers={'Authorization': f"Bearer {os.getenv('QA_TOKEN')}"})
            envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: app-config
            - secretRef:
                name: qa-credentials
            volumeMounts:
            - name: data-volume
              mountPath: /data
            - name: deps-volume
              mountPath: /app/deps
              readOnly: true
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command:
                - python
                - -c
                - "import pandas, jsonschema, requests"
              initialDelaySeconds: 10
              periodSeconds: 5
            livenessProbe:
              exec:
                command:
                - python
                - -c
                - "import sys; sys.exit(0)"
              initialDelaySeconds: 30
              periodSeconds: 30
          - name: cert-rotator
            image: cert-manager/cert-manager-rotator:v1.8.0
            args:
            - --watch-cert-dir=/certs
            - --cert-secret-name=qa-tls-cert
            volumeMounts:
            - name: cert-volume
              mountPath: /certs
          volumes:
          - name: data-volume
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: data-pvc
          - name: deps-volume
            emptyDir: {}
          - name: cert-volume
            emptyDir: {}
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-config
  namespace: example
data:
  SCHEMA_PATH: "/data/schema.json"
  DATE_RANGE: "7"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: qa-credentials
  namespace: example
type: Opaque
data:
  QA_TOKEN: <base64-encoded-token>
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: qa-egress-policy
  namespace: example
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      job-name: data-qa-cronjob
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: qa-namespace
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8090
```

## Trade-offs

**CronJob vs Deployment**: CronJob provides scheduled execution but lacks continuous monitoring. A Deployment could run continuously but would require external coordination.

**InitContainer Pattern**: Ensures dependencies are available but increases startup time and complexity. Using a pre-built image would be faster but reduces flexibility.

**Sidecar for TLS**: Separates concerns and enables independent updates but adds resource overhead and coordination complexity.

**NetworkPolicy Restriction**: Enhances security but requires careful rule management and monitoring to avoid blocking legitimate traffic.

**PVC for Data**: Ensures persistence across runs but creates coupling between namespaces and requires careful capacity planning.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical security hardening and disruption management capabilities for CKAD-level Kubernetes deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Container SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem for container isolation
- PodSecurityContext: fsGroup for proper file permissions on PVC-mounted volumes
- Kernel capabilities: drop ALL to minimize attack surface
- PodDisruptionBudget: maintain minimum healthy pods during maintenance
- Rollout and rollback procedures for safe deployments

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-gateway
  labels:
    app: api-gateway
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: api-gateway
    spec:
      securityContext:
        fsGroup: 1001
      containers:
      - name: api-gateway
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop:
            - "ALL"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /srv
        - name: config
          mountPath: /etc/app
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: api-gateway-pvc
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: api-gateway-config
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: api-gateway-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-gateway
```

## Verification & Rollback
```bash
# Verify under load
kubectl exec deployment/api-gateway -- curl http://localhost:8080/health
kubectl top pods -l app=api-gateway
kubectl get pods -l app=api-gateway --watch

# Rollback if needed
kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-gateway
kubectl rollout status deployment/api-gateway
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests knowledge of namespace-scoped governance primitives (LimitRange, ResourceQuota) and how defaults affect scheduling, QoS, and multi-tenant fairness in CKAD.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace scoping
- LimitRange defaultRequests/defaultLimits
- ResourceQuota hard limits
- Pod scheduling under quotas
- Impact on autoscaling and experimentation

## Code Example
```yaml
# Namespace
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: test-ns
---
# LimitRange
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: default-limits
  namespace: test-ns
spec:
  limits:
  - default:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 256Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    type: Container
---
# ResourceQuota
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: resource-quota
  namespace: test-ns
spec:
  hard:
    pods: "10"
    requests.cpu: "1"
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates CKAD proficiency in extending namespace-centric validation using core Kubernetes primitives: ConfigMaps, Secrets, CronJobs, InitContainers, PVCs, and NetworkPolicies. It also tests knowledge of jq for in-cluster JSON Schema validation and idempotent status updates.

## Key Concepts

- **Namespace-scoped configuration**: All resources operate within a single namespace boundary
- **CronJob with InitContainer tooling**: InitContainer prepares the environment (curl/jq) before the main validation container runs
- **JSON Schema validation using jq**: jq processes ConfigMap data against the fetched schema
- **PVC-backed logging**: Persistent storage preserves logs across job executions
- **NetworkPolicy egress control**: Restricts outbound traffic to only approved endpoints
- **Status persistence in ConfigMap**: Validation results are stored for auditing and downstream consumption

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-config-schema-validator
  namespace: <target-namespace>
spec:
  schedule: "*/7 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: busybox
            command: ["sh", "-c", "wget -O /usr/local/bin/jq https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/download/jq-1.7/jq-linux64 && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/jq"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /usr/local/bin
          containers:
          - name: validator
            image: curlimages/curl:latest
            env:
            - name: API_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: validation-creds
                  key: api-key
            command: ["sh", "-c"]
            args:
            - |
              SCHEMA_URL=$(kubectl get configmap validation-config -o jsonpath='{.data.schema-url}')
              curl -s $SCHEMA_URL -o /logs/schema.json
              for cm in $(kubectl get configmaps -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
                kubectl get configmap $cm -o json | jq -s ".[0] * {data: .[1] | getpath($cm | split(\"-\")[1:] | map(.))}" /logs/schema.json > /logs/validation-$cm.json || true
              done
              curl -X POST http://validation-portal:8080/api/v1/validate -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" --data-binary @/logs/summary.json
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /usr/local/bin
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: validation-logs
          - name: tools
            emptyDir: {}
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Trade-offs

| Aspect | Trade-off |
|--------|-----------|
| **InitContainer vs. Custom Image** | InitContainer adds startup latency but keeps the main image lightweight and avoids maintenance of a custom image. |
| **jq Validation vs. Dedicated Validator** | jq is lightweight and universally available, but lacks full JSON Schema draft support. A dedicated validator (e.g., kubeconform) offers better accuracy at the cost of added complexity. |
| **PVC for Logs** | Provides durability and debugging capability but introduces storage overhead and potential bottlenecks in high-frequency runs. |
| **NetworkPolicy Egress** | Restricts access to only required endpoints, enhancing security but requires careful planning of all dependencies. |
| **ConfigMap Status vs. Custom Resource** | ConfigMap is simpler and requires no CRD management, but lacks built-in versioning and conflict resolution. |

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD ability to implement per-namespace GitOps, use InitContainers, ConfigMaps, PVCs, and NetworkPolicy; validates YAML tooling, apply flow, and status reporting.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace GitOps design patterns
- InitContainer provisioning and tool installation

- Namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy for egress control
- Drift detection and status reporting via ConfigMap

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton for a per-namespace GitOps runner
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gitops-runner
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gitops-runner
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gitops-runner
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: git-clone
        image: alpine/git:latest
        env:
        - name: REPO_URL
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: repo-url
        - name: TARGET_PATH
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: target-path
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          apk add --no-cache git yq
          git clone $(REPO_URL) /workspace/repo
          cd /workspace/repo
          yq eval '.spec.path = "$(TARGET_PATH)"' . > manifests.yaml
      containers:
      - name: validator
        image: kubeval/kubeval:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          kubeval /workspace/manifests.yaml > /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          yamllint -d relaxed /workspace/manifests.yaml >> /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          kubectl apply -f /workspace/manifests.yaml --namespace=$(NAMESPACE)
          kubectl get -f /workspace/manifests.yaml -o jsonpath='{.status}' > /gitops-status
      volumes:
      - name: workspace
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: gitops-logs
```
